newsitem.title: UK: Rank down, report raises property concerns.
newsitem.headline: Rank down, report raises property concerns.

text.p: Shares in Rank Group Plc traded close to their year's low on Monday after a report in the Sunday Telegraph newspaper said a revaluation of the company's property holdings could wipe some 300 million stg off their value.

The stock was down 4-1/2p at 408 by 1128 GMT, near its 12-month low of 396p set on October 31 and little affected by news from the company that it plans to sell its coach holiday business Shearings to a management buy-out team.
Yet analysts said a property revaluation had already been flagged by Rank when it detailed a major reorganisation in August.
"This is not new news," said Matthew Nayler, analyst at Williams de Broe.
In August Rank chief executive Andrew Teare, who took his position three months previously, said he would sell non-core activities and overhaul the company's structure following a strategic review.
The stock has continued to languish since the restructuring statement, reflecting doubts about Teare's strategy, Nayler said.

"It is a question of whether he is going to turn the business for the worse," Nayler said. "My view is that he is going to produce a net improvement and that he is setting about things in the right way. It is a cheap stock."
No-one at Rank was immediately available for comment.
